title: max payne
text: "Smoke rose from the sewers below like all the fires of hell were beneath us." Awesome quotes like that make Max Payne sweet as candy. The game concerns the eponymous hero and tells a peaceful story about his blissful retirement from the NYPD and how he lives happily ever after with his wife and kids. Or not. The game concerns his "Taken style" journey for vengeance after his family are brutally slain by junkies high on a new drug. Valkyrie. The game is (in my mind) split into two seperate parts, the gameplay and the story. The gameplay concerns Max running through new york killing everyone he sees, you use different guns (a lot of them) and have the option of going into bullet time (slowing down time like a family reunion) but fundamentally the gameplay is derivative and repetitive. There's a link with the general pessimisitic film noir tone of the game and how depressed and angry Max is but that doesn't neccessarily excuse gameplay which is so lacking in variety. The story of the game involves tracking down who was responsible for the crime and is told partly through graphic novel style scripts with gritty voiceover, partly through cutscenes using the in-game engine but probably most interestingly through the environment of the game in the form of graffiti, doodads and various TV shows which are variously sinister and funny and educational. The main problem of the game (for me) is (as previously mentioned) the actual gameplay of the game becomes a chore one has to work through to access the storyline (which is interesting and thought provoking). I guess it's kind of like playing an RPG where all the battles seem like a means to the end of enjoying the narrative and you actually wish the game would just be super easy so you could get what you actually want out of it with the minimum of fuss. Overall the game is very interesting and different but has that rather large flaw. Still worth a look.

text: Althought initially I expected this to be another action game, it tunred into something much, much, much better.  Not only is the action top notch quality - especially for it's time, but it's also hitting the limit with it's storytelling and narration through which the player finds out more about the character. The noir feel and the confession of the character is very believable, he tells his monologue through the comixes in the game. The voice acting makes it all the way more enjoyable as a ride through one of those thriller movies.. I really enjoyed this tittle. It's everything you might want from the genre it belongs to, and for 2001 and even today it's an amazing achievement in dark, gothic, violent but very authentic world. I will go at lengths that would advise playing this exclusively. The sequel is not worth it. Can't say anything of Max Payne 3, yet the the second part became a vulgarisation of the worst things action games can offer, poor technical take at new features and bad writing. Severe cases of cultural cliché. As the sequel of the first Bourne movie or the second part of the Matrix. Better to buy a few copies of the original Max Payne for your friends. Games are rarely made this way anymore.

text: After playing through this entire game, i concluded that this game, while old, is still an okay game. The story for Max Payne is hands down ♥♥♥♥ing amazing. It tells the story of Max Payne, an ex-cop that lost his wife and child in a home invasion. This leaves Max Payne depressed and addicted to Pain Killers and Alcohol. This leads Max Payne on a road to revenge as he tracks down the werabouts of the man who killed his loved ones. That sounds good on its own, reading the story is like a book, or a graphic novel. The Gameplay is pretty decent. You run-n-gun your way through repetitive hordes of mafia gangs and eventually, hired private army gunmen. The game is very repetitive. The main draw this game offers is a game mechanic called Bullet Time. Basically, you slow down time to aim better and avoid getting shot, this mechanic is unreliable at times and got me killed alot, though this mechanic is alot better in Max Payne 3 (great game btw). This game actually forces you to think carefully instead of running into a room on mafia/army guards because 1 bullet drains alot of health. Painkillers are used as health and slowly regain your health back. They are very scarce and Iwas always begging for a Painkiller so i didn't die. Thankfully, you can save your game at any point, excluding cutscenes of course. As i said before, i died alot due to the scare of Painkillers, lots of damage obsorbance and the Bullet Time mechanic ♥♥♥♥ing me over. I later found out that this game uses Escalated Diffuculty, meaning that if your doing really well and finding the game too easy, the game bumps up the difficulty without warning, making hard parts already harder. Overall this game is Decent, 6/10 at best but i'm really reccomending this game for its story because i absolutly loved it. 6/10, May Play Again.

text: I recommend this title, but it's not without its problems. The bullet time mechanic is fun and I love the comic book panel cutscenes. However, buyers should be aware that the game is very much a product of its time. The graphics have not aged well and apart from Max, the voice acting is generally bad and a lot of the dialogue is cringe inducing. The game lacks any kind of auto-save system and there are no checkpoints, so you must remember to save often. There is also no controller support, which is admittedly only a minor issue, but it's still worth noting. Some players might notice wonky sound, but this can be fixed with patches. Overall, it's pretty good and is a definite must-play for retro-gaming enthusiasts or fans of noir-style storytelling.

title: max payne 3
text: More video than game.  Skip it.  The number and frequency of cut-scenes is absolutely obscene.  The most obnoxious of any game I've ever played.  It completely ruins pace and momentum in order to hide poor level design. The gameplay that's there is decent.  When you don't need to take cover to survive and can use bullet-time (which has been rolled back from what it was in Max Payne 2) the combat feels fun and engaging.  However, every single thing you do is interrupted by in-game or recorded cut scenes.  Which are unskippable. On top of this, the game is plagued by a VHS and after-image effect which makes no sense in the context of the story, its characters, or the presentation.  There is no rhyme or reason to this effect, just a frequency which bests Max's unending monologues.  What was completely endearing in the first two games has become, with Max Payne 3, a crutch which ruins the original charm and overstays its welcome.  What was once a treat now feels like a punishment. I wouldn't even recommend this game on a steep discount.  Play Max Payne 2, instead.

Constant cutscenes, interruptions to player control, limited movement, limited weapon slots, extremely linear level design and pathways, nothing worthwhile to unlock after you beat the game, which isn't even challenging... forget it. Put the 20 dollars in your gas tank or save your money for a better game. Nothing to see here.

text: TL/DR - On it's own terms, I'd give it a 8/10 with a 6/10 overall. NTL/R: Gather round, children, and I'll tell you a tell of gaming in the year of our lord nineteen hundred and eigthy four.  You see, back then, games HAD to rely on uniqueness to stand out.  Some where unique by having great graphics, others through innovative game play, while still others by challenge and re-playability.  In this age there came a game, on an ancient machine known only as a C64, a game called "Cliff Hanger".  It had the audacity to stand out by having something of a sense of humour and somewhat hazy rules that you had to suss out through exploration.   Comprised of a "scene", each level had to be explored and the rules and ways of beating it had to be discovered.  Failure simply meant that you watched fail animation that kind of made you smile.  And then this idea was lost to time, not quite enough to become legend, not too little to be utterly forgotten by those who were there. Lost, that is, until now. is a game about failure.  It's a game about exploration, and, ultimately, a game that you will step away from glad that you bought it.  The humour is on point, the presentation is solid, the music is engaging, and game play in interesting; it is worth the money the dev is charging.  It's not going to affect you, or change how you see gaming or narriative, or any of this, it's just solid, fun, silly game play. Pros ---- - The graphical style is great retro-inspired chunky pixels - It's pretty comical, with surprising outcomes for various actions - Simple, stupid, fun Cons ----- - Once you've beaten it, you're probably not going back - It's definitely not for everyone.  Hardcores will probably not enjoy it at all. There's really not much more to be said about it.  On it's own terms, I'd give it a 8/10.

title: men of war: assault squad
text: Well, everyone round here knows I love (or rather love/hate thanks to the many bugs) all of the Men of War series - and Faces of War. "Assault Squad" is no different. But I have to declare that gameplay wise, this one is the weakest of the series, yet technically it's one of the most sturdy and bug free (don't worry, many old favourite bugs even from FoW's day are *still* hanging in there)! The opposite to "Condemed Heroes" and "Red Tide" which had the best gameplay, interesting story and well designed missions, but teeming with bugs! One simple reason for the low gameplay score..... the most lazy, half-arsed scenario design I have ever seen! ALL 5 campaigns for each nation are just literally cut & paste copies of each other..... getting all the DLCs for MOW:AS is also a must - when they're on a good offer that is! They at least introduce a few new types of scenarios - including a special "Xmas" one! The other fault, and evidence of lazy programming, is the "sod doing any more work than needed, let's just give the AI infinite respawns and infinate RPs" attitude. This makes for some very long winded, exhausting scenarios - which you will have to play on permanent slo-mo mode just in order to keep up! The game is heavily biased toward LAN/Internet play and people who will build their own scenarios. There are no "script heavy storyline" missions like in the other MoWs! Taken on their own individual merits, these skirmish style are OK, but the repitition gets very, very old, very, very quick! Being a stubborn smacktard, I still went and worked through them all! "1C" still have not been bothered to supply proper AI bots that can be used in LAN/Internet play. They've left that for Assault Squad 2, as a STUPIDLY overpriced DLC - which many report doesn't even work. What next, "Pause Mode DLC" for £19.99? Better not give "1C" any ideas - it's looking like they are all turning into David "Robber" Brabens! The best thing is, the modding community! There's tons of mods available, you are far from stuck with "1C"'s repetitive scenarios!
